R065-01.notes: Narrator chooses the linkage replacement (P4), then calls back for 'Cleaning only' (P6). B: narrator never learns repair or opens a business. C: the mother wanted to give it away, but there is no argument and the narrator keeps it. D: the e's in the letters match the machine ('The same lift'), so the letters were typed on this machine.

R065-02.notes: P3: 'replace the whole linkage... it will never stick again.' A: it cost three times as much as the cleaning. B: color is never mentioned. D: timing is never mentioned.

R065-03.notes: The bar 'hung there a beat too long... unless I waited', and the companion 'kept stopping', so the typing kept pausing. A is the intended trap: window-shopping sounds leisurely, but the point is the interruption. C: the problem is delay, not speed. D overstates; the machine 'worked, mostly'.

R065-04.notes: 'Respectful' implies respect toward the inherited object and Vesna. A: nothing suggests Pellerin would be offended; he 'nodded'. B: nothing says cleaning would cause damage. C: the mother's expectations are never mentioned; she wanted to give the typewriter away.

R065-05.notes: 'For comparison... Afterward', and the narrator does lay 'Mr. Pellerin's line beside hers.' B: nothing suggests he doubted payment. C: the machine still types, and his line was legible enough to compare. D: he typed 'slowly'.

R065-06.notes: 'did not sound surprised', together with the comparison sheet he prepared, implies he anticipated the change. A contradicts 'not surprised'. B: he says it 'will still stick a little', which means cleaning helps but leaves the quirk, not that it fails entirely. D: unsupported, and he readily agrees to cleaning only.

R065-07.notes: Pellerin types slowly so that each sticking type bar can fully return to its rest position before the next key, as P2 describes ('unless I waited'). A and C are literal readings of 'home'. D: the point is waiting, not force. Some takers may read 'come home' as the e fully striking the paper, but no option says that, so B is the only defensible choice.

R065-08.notes: The sticking e is the 'lift' that appears in Vesna's letters, so replacing the linkage would 'erase her' trace in the machine. A: the passage never mentions insulting his cleaning skill. B and C: the existing letters and carbon copies would be unaffected. D echoes the word 'erase' from the passage, but that is ordinary paraphrase, not a giveaway.

R065-09.notes: 'forty years of carbon copies, one for every letter she had sent.' A: they are Vesna's own letters, not the narrator's. C: the letters were sent, not unmailed drafts. D: Pellerin's single sheet is a separate item.

R065-10.notes: 'asked for it before I knew why... not sure I could explain myself.' A: the passage shows no regret, and the mother wanted to give it away, not keep it. B: it is 'faintly ridiculous beside my laptop', not matching. D: the narrator does use it, and 'indifferent' contradicts asking for it.
